analysis.evidence: אֶת־הַשִּׂמְלָה identifies the garment as the direct object. Shem and Japheth then put it on their shoulders, confirming that they first took it in hand.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ marks a Qal wayyiqtol. The verb is third-person masculine singular and precedes the compound subject שֵׁם וָיֶפֶת, agreeing with its first member.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁם וָיֶפֶת names Shem and Japheth as the pair who take the garment. שְׁנֵיהֶם (“both of them”) refers back to the pair, and אֲבִיהֶם (“their father”) identifies the man they cover as their father.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Shem, son of Noah and brother of Japheth.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁם וָיֶפֶת names Shem and Japheth together. שְׁנֵיהֶם (“the two of them”) refers to the brothers who carry the garment and cover their father.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וָ means “and” and joins the personal name יֶפֶת to שֵׁם.
Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Shem and Japheth take הַשִּׂמְלָה, “the garment,” which supplies the understood object of וַיָּשִׂימוּ. The phrase עַל שְׁכֶם שְׁנֵיהֶם specifies where they laid it, across their shoulders.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural. The subject is Shem and Japheth.
analysis.sense: place something at a specified location

analysis.evidence: Shem and Japheth place the garment עַל שְׁכֶם שְׁנֵיהֶם, “on the shoulders of the two of them,” then walk backward to cover their father. The phrase identifies where each brother carries the garment.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state before שְׁנֵיהֶם, “the two of them.” The singular refers to one shoulder of each brother.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 66311:2, 66073:1.
analysis.morphology: Masculine dual cardinal numeral in the construct state with a third-person masculine plural pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: Shem and Japheth put the garment on their shoulders and walked to cover their father. The following adverb אֲחֹרַנִּית specifies that they walked backward.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, with Shem and Japheth as its subject.
analysis.sense: go, move from place to place

analysis.evidence: וַיֵּלְכוּ אֲחֹרַנִּית means “they walked backward.” Shem and Japheth approached their father with their faces turned away so they could cover him without seeing his nakedness.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew adverb of direction modifying וַיֵּלְכוּ.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67862:4, 66061:6, 66059:5, 65793:3.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.
